_README: canonical_spec.json -- the single frozen definition of what 'canonical' means.
Read by code/more/run_context.py:assert_not_silent_proxy(). A training run may
only declare logging.experiment_group == 'canonical_phase_b' if:
(a) every non-null field in enforced_fields matches its resolved config,
(b) every non-null field in architecture_variants[<its architecture>]
matches -- only ITS OWN block is consulted,
(c) resolve_variant() returns 'canonical' (no ablation is active),
(d) it uses the full dataset and names a seed from seed_set.
A null value means NOT YET FROZEN, and the guard refuses any canonical claim
that depends on it. This is deliberate (plan.md Gate 0: 'final experiments
cannot silently use proxy settings'). A null in enforced_fields blocks ALL
canonical runs; a null in one architecture_variants block blocks only that
architecture.
T8.2 STRUCTURE NOTE -- why the loss weights are NOT in enforced_fields.
config.py:apply_architecture legitimately zeroes some of them per
architecture: MoE has no recursion so halting=0.0, MoR has one expert so
routing_balance=0.0 and step_routing=0.0. Before T8.2, routing_balance sat in
enforced_fields; the moment it was frozen to 0.001 the guard would have
refused every canonical MoR run, because MoR resolves it to 0.0 by design.
That would have blocked one third of the Phase 9 matrix with a message that
looked like a config error. Anything apply_architecture varies belongs below.
T8.2 PROVENANCE NOTE -- how these values were arrived at, per field, so the
paper can state it honestly. See frozen_by. Three of them
(d_model / lr / weight_decay) are VALIDATED-STABLE, not sweep-selected: no
comparative hyperparameter search was run. They are frozen because 12
completed 20-epoch runs at these values converge stably to val task loss
~0.0635 with no divergence or dead experts. Do not write them up as a tuned
optimum.

frozen_by.num_blocks: plan.md Phase 8 (Section 10) - one recursive MoRE block initially
frozen_by.train_split_version: Phase 1 - fixed train/val/test files, not a re-split per run
frozen_by.d_model: T8.2 VALIDATED-STABLE, not sweep-selected. 12 completed 20-epoch runs (actdec x6, routedec x6) converge to val task loss ~0.0635 with no divergence. No comparative width sweep was run; do not report as tuned.
frozen_by.lr: T8.2 VALIDATED-STABLE, not sweep-selected. Same 12 runs, AdamW + CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=epochs). No lr sweep was run under the corrected Top-1/ACT/normalized-balance regime.
frozen_by.weight_decay: T8.2 VALIDATED-STABLE, not sweep-selected. Same 12 runs. No wd sweep was run.
frozen_by.dropout: Inherited unchanged through Phases 2-6; every gate and every 20-epoch run above used 0.1.
frozen_by.grad_clip: Inherited unchanged; no gradient-norm blowup observed in any Phase 2-6 run.
frozen_by.max_steps: Dataset property, not a hyperparameter - programs are packed with 7 step-tokens (data/script.py).
frozen_by.step_feat_dim: Dataset property - 12 features per step-token, leakage-audited (T8.5).
frozen_by.routing_mode: updated_rules.md 1.1 / plan.md 4.1. Dense evaluate-all-and-blend is ablation F and may never be canonical.
frozen_by.router_noise: updated_rules.md 2.5 / plan.md 7.4. Canonical default is none; noise is ablation D.
frozen_by.halting_mode: T8.0a controlled ACT decision experiment, 3 seeds x 2 arms x 20 epochs. pure_act 0.063676 +/- 0.000283 vs supervised_curriculum 0.063953 +/- 0.000190; gap -0.000277 is inside the seed std, so the pre-registered tie rule selected the less-supervised arm. supervised_curriculum remains available as a labelled ablation.
frozen_by.task_weight: loss_weights.task = 1.0 is the reference scale every other weight is expressed against; it is not tuned.
frozen_by.family_cls_weight: T8.3. Frozen at the value every run in the project's history actually used -- it was a bare 0.5 literal inside engine.py's total_loss until T8.3, so it is INHERITED, not selected: no sweep or ablation informed it. It is external annotation (data/script.py stamps a 'family' string per record; more/data.py reads it off disk), it is the second-largest term in the objective, and it is shared by all three architectures, which is why it sits here and not in architecture_variants. 0.0 is the labelled T10.H no_family_supervision ablation. Do not write it up as a tuned coefficient.

_note: T8.2: these ARE now enforced by the Gate 0 guard, and only the block whose
name equals the run's `architecture` is consulted. `top1_routing` is the one
exception -- it is descriptive only, because the enforceable facts behind it
are `routing_mode` (shared, enforced above) and `num_experts` (enforced
here); MoR's false is a consequence of num_experts=1, not a separate switch.
T8.3 -- mor.ffn_mult is RESOLVED at 24 (was null). The parameter-budget
policy is: equalise the TOTAL FFN hidden width, not the per-FFN multiplier.
MoR has one FFN where MoRE has six, so the shared multiplier 4 gives MoR
571,150 params against MoRE's 3,201,555 -- an 82.2% shortfall that fails
T9.2's 5% budget-matching bound outright, and would have made every
MoE/MoR/MoRE loss comparison a comparison of model sizes. 24 = 4 x 6 gives
MoR's single FFN the total hidden width of MoRE's six experts; it is
principled rather than fitted. Measured (T8.3, after the label heads were
0.12%), 25 -> 3,329,038 (gap 3.98%). The 0.12% residual is the router and
the six per-expert halt heads that MoR does not have; it is irreducible by
any integer multiplier and is reported, not hidden.
ffn_mult 4 REMAINS AVAILABLE as the labelled under-budgeted small baseline
(variant tag ffn_mult_4, T10.I). It answers a different question -- what MoR
does at MoRE's per-expert width -- and may appear in an ablation table with
the parameter count printed beside it, never in the headline comparison.
See PHASE11_AUDIT.md.

architecture_variants_frozen_by.num_experts: updated_rules.md 2 / plan.md 7.2 - six families E1..E6, E7 catch-all removed. MoR is 1 by definition (no routing decision).
architecture_variants_frozen_by.max_depth: plan.md Section 10 - recursion budget 7, matching max_steps. MoE is 1 by definition (no recursion).
architecture_variants_frozen_by.adaptive_halting: Definitional: MoR and MoRE have ACT halting, MoE does not.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.ffn_mult: moe/more: 4, unchanged since the field was introduced (T6.7). mor: 24, RESOLVED at T8.3 by equalising total FFN hidden width (4 x 6 experts). Measured gap to MoRE 0.12%, inside T9.2's 5% bound; 23 and 25 give 4.22% and 3.98%. See architecture_variants._note. ffn_mult 4 for MoR is the labelled ffn_mult_4 small-baseline ablation, not canonical.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.routing_balance_weight: T4.2 measurement, frozen at 0.001 (weighted balance term at 0.017x task loss post-warmup, hard expert load spread 9.5-29.3%). MoR 0.0: nothing to balance with one expert.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.step_routing_weight: T8.0b / plan.md E. 0.0 = canonical. Non-zero trains the router against the oracle expert index and is the T10.E oracle-routing ablation. Measured cost of removing the oracle: -0.000155 val task loss against a 0.000428 seed std, i.e. inside noise.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.halting_weight: Ponder cost 0.001. MoE 0.0: max_depth 1 means every token forced-exits at step 1, so a ponder cost would be a constant.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.halting_supervision_weight: 0.0 everywhere - the T8.0a decision is pure ACT. Non-zero is the labelled supervised_curriculum ablation.

_README: Comparison protocol for the Phase 9 headline matrix. These fields are NOT
in enforced_fields and the Gate 0 guard does not check them -- they are the
written-down rules the protocol audit (plan.md step 3) requires, recorded
here so there is one source of truth instead of a convention held only in a
changelog entry.
Changing val_interval changes config_hash, so it must be set BEFORE the
matrix launches; a mid-matrix change produces two hash groups that may not
share a table.
protocol.val_interval_note: logging.log_interval in config.json. Gates validation in engine.py. Raised from 10 to 2 at T9.0: at 10 a 20-epoch run measured val twice, so checkpoint_selection had two candidates and always returned the last epoch on a still-falling curve.
protocol.checkpoint_selection_note: AMENDED AT T11.0b. Was 'lowest val/task_loss among evaluated epochs'. The old rule's own note required re-checking, on the matrix, whether the argmin coincided with the final epoch as it had on the six 20-epoch T10.H runs. Re-checked: it does NOT -- all 15 canonical Phase B runs diverge. That forced a choice, and last-epoch is the defensible one: best_val_loss is a minimum over the ~13 evaluated epochs, i.e. an order statistic whose downward bias grows with an arm's per-epoch validation noise, and that noise is NOT matched across arms (MoR 0.000052 vs MoE 0.000194 per-seed std). Selecting on it would hand the noisiest arm the largest free improvement -- a selection bias that varies by architecture, which is exactly what a three-way comparison cannot tolerate. Last-epoch is noisier per run but unbiased and identically defined for every arm. Fixed epoch count with no early stopping makes it well defined. Verified harmless to the conclusion: every pairwise verdict in the matrix is identical under both rules (see PHASE11_AUDIT.md 7.1), so this amendment changes the declared protocol, not any finding. best_val_loss is still recorded in metrics.json and may be reported as a secondary column, never as the primary.
protocol.parameter_budget_policy: equalise total FFN hidden width, not per-FFN multiplier
protocol.parameter_budget_note: MoR has one FFN where MoE/MoRE have six, so MoR ffn_mult = 24 = 4 x 6. Residual gap 0.120% (MoR 3,197,710 vs 3,201,555) decomposes EXACTLY into three parts, corrected at T11.0b: 1,285 for the six per-expert halt heads MoR does not have, 1,280 for the router, and 1,280 in FFN BIASES -- the component the pre-T11.0b version of this note omitted. Six experts carry 6 x (1024 + 256) = 7,680 bias parameters against MoR's single 6144 + 256 = 6,400. The weight MATRICES match to the parameter (6 x 2 x 256 x 1024 = 2 x 256 x 6144); only the biases cannot be equalised, and they cannot be at any integer multiplier. The gap runs AGAINST the headline result -- MoR wins on val/task_loss with fewer parameters -- so it cannot be the explanation. State it, never hide it. Separately: MoE and MoRE are parameter-identical to the unit (3,201,555 both), because adaptive_halting is not a MoREModel constructor argument, so the six halt heads are allocated under architecture=moe as well and simply never receive gradient. That makes MoRE-vs-MoE the exactly-matched isolation of recursion.
protocol.seed_reporting: mean +- std over the full seed_set; verdicts come from the exact two-sided randomization test in code/seed_stats.py, never from a k x std threshold
protocol.seed_reporting_note: AMENDED AT T11.0b. Was 'a difference smaller than the seed std is not a difference'. That rule, and the 2x variant used in practice, compares a difference of MEANS against the spread of a SINGLE arm's seeds. The correct denominator is the standard error of the difference, sqrt(s_a^2/n_a + s_b^2/n_b), which at n=5 per arm is about sqrt(5) smaller -- so the old rule was roughly sqrt(n) too CONSERVATIVE and was suppressing real results. It suppressed two: MoR-vs-MoRE in the matrix ('1.93x, noise'; actually 3.94 standard errors, p = 0.0159) and both the dense_routing and routing_supervision Phase 10 arms. Replaced with exact enumeration rather than a re-tuned k: at 5-vs-5 there are only C(10,5) = 252 regroupings of the pooled values, so the null distribution is computed exactly -- deterministic, no normality assumption, no threshold to justify. ALWAYS report the resolution floor 1/C(n_a+n_b, n_a) alongside p: 0.0040 at 5v5, 0.0179 at 3v5, 0.0500 at 3v3. A p equal to the floor means the observed split is the single most extreme arrangement the design admits, which is a weaker statement than 'significant' and does not survive Bonferroni at six arms. Do NOT use the paired sign-flip variant here: 2^5 = 32 sign assignments give a minimum two-sided p of 0.0625, which can never reach alpha = 0.05, and pairing is weakly motivated anyway because train_split_version = fixed-file-splits-v1 fixes the split, so a seed varies only initialisation and shuffle order. The old necessary condition is still computed and reported as gap_over_std so it can be checked; it is not the verdict.
protocol.primary_metric_floor_note: predict-the-train-mean on the real val split (n=5250). Read val/task_loss against this, never against 0.
